group.passage:
Sneakers (or trainers for the British) for modern people are not just for sports, but have become a fashion statement. A look at how they evolve may shed some light on how they become a staple for the masses. In the 1830s, John Boyd Dunlop created the earliest sports shoes, called the plimsolls, with canvas uppers and rubber soles. These shoes were good for beach outings in the Victorian era, so they were also called sandshoes. Yet, they were pretty crude—no difference between the left and right foot.
In the late nineteen century, the industrial revolution not only changed people’s way of work but also popularized sports events, leading to a boom in the sports shoe business. In 1916, 30 different plimsoll companies were merged by the US Rubber Company, which then rolled out Keds. Because the soft rubber sole of Keds allowed wearers to walk without making any noise and thus sneak up on others, they were also known as sneakers. The next year, Converse released the All Star series, bearing the name of the Indiana hoop star Chuck Taylor, who kickstarted the trend of sports celebrities endorsing shoe brands. With hardened cap protecting the wearers’ toes and the high top shielding the ankles, the Converse plimsolls dominated the shoe market in the early 20th century. Not only did the US and UK armies adopt them as standard kits, but teens also embraced them as fashionable accessories.
In 1936, as the American basketball team wore Converse in the Berlin Olympics, US runner Jesse Owen took home four gold medals wearing shoes designed by Rudolf and Adolf Dassler brothers. The brothers later parted, continuing to prove themselves in the sportswear market, with Rudolf founding Puma and Adolf establishing Adidas. By the 1950s, sneakers had become synonymous with youth and fashion, widely accepted by young people for their comfort and casual styles. Then in the 1970s, Nike joined the sportswear game, not just improving athletic performances, but also elevating the sports gear from functional purposes to objects of obsessions. In 1984, Michael Jordan was signed to wear Nike shoes, Air Jordans, the most famous sneakers in history.
Whether in sports or in the fashion world, sneakers have been and will always be a cultural icon and personal fashion statement.

figures.label: 第1題選項(A)–(D)圖片
figures.caption: 第1題四個選項皆為鞋子的黑白照片（去背）
figures.description: 四張黑白去背照片，由左至右為選項(A)–(D)。(A) 一雙白色花式溜冰鞋：高筒皮靴、靴口高過腳踝、前方密集鞋帶孔，鞋底裝有冰刀。(B) 一隻白色低筒帆布鞋（側面）：白色鞋帶、鞋頭有白色橡膠護片，橡膠鞋底一圈有兩道深色細條紋；鞋口低，不包覆腳踝。(C) 一雙深灰色低筒帆布鞋：深色鞋帶、白色橡膠鞋底，鞋頭為與鞋身同色的帆布，沒有明顯的橡膠鞋頭護片；鞋口低，不包覆腳踝。(D) 一隻白色高筒帆布鞋（側面）：鞋口高過腳踝（腳踝內側有圓形貼片）、白色鞋帶、鞋頭有白色橡膠護片，橡膠鞋底一圈有兩道深色細條紋。

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following pictures is a pair of Converse All Star series?

options.A: ［圖］一雙白色花式溜冰鞋（高筒皮靴，鞋底裝有冰刀）。
options.B: ［圖］一隻白色低筒帆布鞋：鞋頭有橡膠護片，鞋底有兩道深色條紋，鞋口不包覆腳踝。
options.C: ［圖］一雙深灰色低筒帆布鞋：白色橡膠鞋底，沒有明顯的橡膠鞋頭護片，鞋口不包覆腳踝。
options.D: ［圖］一隻白色高筒帆布鞋：鞋口高過腳踝（腳踝處有圓形貼片），鞋頭有橡膠護片，鞋底有兩道深色條紋。

questions.stem:
In what order did the following shoes or shoes brands appear?
a. Adidas
b. Converse All Star series
c. Keds
d. plimsolls
From this passage, what can we learn about sports shoes?

options.A: The industrial revolution played a role in the creation of the earliest sports shoes.
options.B: Sneakers are thus named because wearers can creep behind others quickly.
options.C: Chuck Taylor started the trend of sports stars promoting shoes.
options.D: Wearers of the earliest sports shoes would have to distinguish between left and right shoes.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is true about the development of sports shoes in the 20th century?

options.A: The youth identified themselves with the trendy and cozy feel of the sneakers.
options.B: The Berlin Olympics was the show room for Converse and Adidas.
options.C: Nike’s Air Jordans series were the best-selling shoes in history.
options.D: Sports shoes were mainly worn for activities on the beach.
